newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS UPDATE - MAY 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS UPDATE - MAY 5.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The International Monetary Fund will begin its 10-day evaluation of the success of Prime Minister Costas Simitis's economic policies today: the evaluation is taking place at a particularly crucial time for the government. On the plus side, however, the government will point to falling inflation and interest rates and increased economic activity and public investment.

--One-third of Greek industries was able to improve its real prices, sales and profits in 1996, according to a new study. The leading Greek enterprise was food and beverage industry Chipita International.
--Ten Athens Stock Exchange listed companies are facing fines of up to 100 million drachmas for their involvement in the Delta scandal, sources report.

--The merger of pensions funds for banks, the establishment of a mutual fund to handle the capital of this new fund and the examination of the possibility of merging more funds are the three main axes of the government's "small package" of reforms to the social insurance sector. These issues will be the focus of talks at the same time as changes to the job market begin being discussed between government, unions and employers on May 14.

--The introduction of the euro will mean far-reaching changes for business and worker. The most appparent changes will be felt first by export and tourist-related companies and by banks, with the shrinking of traditional activities.

--Companies listed on the Athens Stock Exchange are expecting significant improvements in returns for this year. An Omega study on some 110 listed firms has predicted returns up by 25-30 percent over 1996 figures.

--All firms will now be required to be issued certificates proving that they are up to date on their employee pension contributions, part of efforts by the government to combat tax evasion. The new measure is one of five expected to included in a comprehensive bill to be submitted to Parliament soon.

--The Athens bourse is leading the list of up-and-coming stock exchange markets this year, with foreign investors placing 1.4 billion dollars with the bourse, and beating out the neighbouring competitors and the growing industrial superhouses of the Near East and Latin America.
--Four-fifths of ASE members have informed the authorities that they will announce increased dividends for their share-holders for 1996.

--A series of meetings begins this week at the national economy ministry on the issue of financing investments in infrastructural works in the Balkans with the participation of major international organisations such as the International Monetary Fund and investment houses Morgan Stanley and Salomon Brothers. Greece's participation will be led by the National Bank.
--Monday will also see Mytilineos signing its agreement with Yugoslav companies on the handling of mines in Kosovo and Serbia.
